meaning: The number 276 is mentioned in Acts 27:37 as the count of people on board the ship during Paul's shipwreck, symbolizing God's providence and salvation.
description: In Acts 27:37 it is recorded that there were 276 people on board when the ship sank while en route to Rome, and all survived just as Paul had prophesied. The number has been interpreted as a symbol of God's complete care and protection over every soul, regardless of quantity. This specific figure underscores Luke's eyewitness account and historical accuracy, testifying that God keeps His word down to the smallest detail—not one soul was lost.

footnotes.text: The ship was likely a large grain vessel from Alexandria of the type used to transport grain from Egypt to Rome. Such ships could be up to 55 meters long and accommodate several hundred passengers, making the number 276 historically credible.

In Jewish gematria, the number 276 has no prominent independent symbolic meaning, though some have noted that it is the triangular number of 23 (the sum of all numbers from 1 to 23), without this being assigned any established theological interpretation.
